name: WinZO
tagline: Vernacular real-money casual games app, collapsed after ban and ED action
facts: 2018, Saumya Singh Rathore and Paavan Nanda
Private; backers incl. Griffin, Kalaari, Makers Fund
ED froze ₹500–800 cr; founders arrested Nov 2025
ED chargesheet Jan 2026; both founders on bail

strategy.label: Mission
strategy.text: Pre-ban: bring Bharat's 'desi' casual games (Ludo, Carrom, Rummy) online with small cash stakes in 12 languages.

strategy.label: Old model
strategy.text: Platform fee on micro-stake peer contests across 100+ games, plus a developer program letting studios list real-money games.

strategy.label: Ban response
strategy.text: Shut cash games, launched ZO TV short video, micro-dramas, digital gold and free games; pushed into US, Brazil, Germany.

strategy.label: Enforcement
strategy.text: ED alleges bots against users, ₹43 cr unrefunded balances, $55M routed to US shell, overseas RMG run from India.

strategy.label: Lesson
strategy.text: Regulatory risk is existential: governance, user-fund segregation and honest matchmaking matter more than growth when rules change.

strategy.label: Your view
strategy.text: Was WinZO's pivot doomed because its audience valued winning money, or because trust collapsed under enforcement?

customers.pain: Want quick fun and small winnings on low-end phones
customers.why: Familiar desi games, ₹1-level stakes, vernacular UI, fast UPI payouts (pre-ban)

customers.pain: Withdrawals delayed or blocked; ₹43 cr allegedly unrefunded
customers.why: Stayed only to recover funds; trust largely gone

customers.who: Indian indie studios in WinZO program
customers.pain: Hard to monetise casual games and reach Bharat users
customers.why: Distribution to crore-scale users and revenue share on contests (pre-ban)

customers.pain: Want social skill games with prizes
customers.why: Expansion bet post-ban; ED says these ran from Indian entity

customers.who: Paytm and ad networks, payment gateways
customers.why: Was a top ad spender; Paytm later sued for ₹3.6 cr dues

Margin on gold buy/sell via partner vault

bullets.label: Revenue mix
bullets.text: Pre-ban almost entirely contest fees; FY24 ₹1,055 cr. Post-ban revenue near zero, accounts unfiled.

bullets.label: Users vs payers
bullets.text: Claimed ~25 cr users; a small paying minority drove rake. Free users monetise far worse.

bullets.label: Unit economics
bullets.text: Profitable pre-ban (adj. PAT ₹315 cr) on cheap Bharat CAC; ED alleges bots inflated house wins.

bullets.label: Liquidity
bullets.text: ₹500–800 cr frozen by ED, ~₹15 cr usable cash; vendors and Paytm pursuing dues.

bullets.label: Growth levers
bullets.text: Realistically survival: unfreeze funds, settle refunds, win cases; then ads-led content or overseas apps.

friction: Withdrawals frozen; users cannot access remaining balances
Bot opponents allegedly undisclosed, destroying fairness trust
Free games offer no reason to stay without winnings
ZO TV pivot unrelated to core gaming habit
Founder arrests and frozen accounts stall product shipping
